newsitem.title: USA: Baxter gets FDA surgery system clearance.
newsitem.headline: Baxter gets FDA surgery system clearance.

text.p: Baxter Healthcare Corp said Wednesday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has cleared its Side Branch Occlusion (SBO) System for marketing in the United States.
Baxter, a unit of Baxter International Inc, said the system allows vascular surgeons to perform minimally invasive surgery to treat peripheral vascular disease.

Nearly two million Americans suffer from the disease, Baxter said in a statement. Cholesterol plaque deposits form in arteries, decreasing blood-carrying capacity. The disease is the leading cause of amputations in the United States, Baxter said.

Traditional treatment requires surgery in which an incision running the length of the patient's leg, from the groin to the ankle, is made. Baxter said its SBO system requires two minor incisions, one at the groin and one below the knee.
Baxter International is a global medical-products and services company.
